assessment.nobel_worthiness: Magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene opened moire quantum materials: a theoretically predicted flat-band condition leading to correlated insulators and superconductivity in a controllable, tunable system. The field is a genuine new platform for strongly interacting electrons with broad impact on many-body physics.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald made the continuum-model prediction of flat bands at the magic angle (2011); Jarillo-Herrero's group made the decisive 2018 experimental discovery of correlated insulators and superconductivity. Theory plus experiment gives a natural three-person configuration; the experimental side is shared with the Cory Dean and Pablo group literature, and I take the exact credited names only.
assessment.maturity: Independently reproduced by many groups worldwide within a few years, with a large and stable literature. The core phenomenology is secure although the microscopic pairing mechanism remains debated; recognition is timely rather than premature.
uncertainties: Pairing mechanism of the superconductivity is unresolved
Credit between early theory (including others not listed) and the 2018 experiments may be contested
Possible overlap with other moire platforms and 2D magnetism candidates

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks, built on Katori's magic-wavelength proposal, reached 1e-18 fractional uncertainty and now redefine what precision measurement can test, from relativistic redshift across millimetres to searches for new physics. Clear, original and of lasting impact for metrology.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed and first demonstrated the magic-wavelength lattice scheme; Ye's group drove the strontium clock to record accuracy and many-body-controlled performance. Two names give a clean allocation, though other groups (e.g. Lemonde, Ludlow, Hinkley) contributed and are not on the list.
assessment.maturity: Multiple independent clocks across the world agree and are used for international comparisons; the redefinition of the second is under discussion. Mature and timely.
uncertainties: Thorium-229 and ion clocks could compete for credit in the same area
Relative weight of Ye's contributions versus the broader frequency-comb heritage already recognised in 2005

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Experimental discovery of the Higgs boson at the LHC confirmed the last missing piece of the Standard Model and is a landmark of experimental physics; importance and clarity are beyond doubt.
assessment.attribution: The 2013 prize went to Englert and Higgs for theory. The experimental recognition must rest on a limited set of leaders of the proposal and construction of ATLAS and CMS; the credited three are the founding spokespersons or leaders, but the discovery was made by thousands and any selection is partly arbitrary.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed independently by two experiments and subsequently by precision coupling measurements; interpretation is stable. Recognition is overdue rather than premature.
uncertainties: Attribution to individuals for a collaboration discovery is contentious
Statutes limit to three people while the experimental leadership is larger
Whether the committee wants to honour management over detector-physics contributions

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Kardar-Parisi-Zhang equation defines a universality class for non-equilibrium interface growth and, via exact solutions, links to random-matrix statistics (Tracy-Widom) and quantum spin chains. Its experimental confirmation in turbulent liquid crystals (Takeuchi) closed the gap between theory and experiment. As a statistical physicist I regard it as a fundamental and strikingly original achievement.
assessment.attribution: Kardar and Zhang (with Parisi, who already holds a prize for other work) wrote the 1986 equation; Takeuchi provided clean experimental verification of the universal distributions. Exact solutions by Johansson, Spohn, Sasamoto, Amir-Corwin-Quastel and others are not credited here and form an unresolved allocation issue.
assessment.maturity: Experimental evidence has strengthened over fifteen years, including recent measurements in spin chains and cold atoms, but the field is still actively evolving. Timing is reasonable for a long-recognised theory.
uncertainties: Mathematical solutions carry significant credit that falls outside the list
Parisi's earlier laureate status complicates a natural three-person configuration
Experimental confirmation is limited to specific systems

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ultracold atoms in optical lattices realise Hubbard models with controllable parameters, enabling observation of the superfluid-Mott transition, single-site resolution and quantum simulation of many-body states. Broad importance for many-body physics.
assessment.attribution: Zoller (with Jaksch) provided key theoretical proposals; Greiner and Bloch performed the Mott-insulator experiment, Esslinger the fermionic realisations. I choose three experimentalists but the theory-experiment balance is delicate and the list has four names.
assessment.maturity: Reproduced widely and now a mature platform; quantum simulation beyond classical reach is still developing, so the strongest implications are not fully settled.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2001 and 2012 prizes on cold atoms
Credit for theory proposals (Zoller, Jaksch) versus experimental demonstrations
Practical advantage over classical simulation still debated

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit QED made strong coupling of artificial atoms to microwave photons routine and underpins superconducting quantum processors and dispersive readout. Highly influential, following the 2025 prize on macroscopic quantum effects in circuits.
assessment.attribution: Blais, Huang, Wallraff, Girvin and Schoelkopf wrote the 2004 proposal; Wallraff and Schoelkopf demonstrated strong coupling. I name Girvin as theory leader alongside the two experimental leaders, leaving Blais out in a four-person list, which is a judgement call.
assessment.maturity: Reproduced across the world and technologically central; however, close recognition of the 2025 prize may argue for waiting.
uncertainties: Proximity to the 2025 prize in the same community
Proper division of theory credit between Blais and Girvin
Whether quantum-computing relevance is mature enough

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Predicting and observing the quantum spin Hall effect and topological insulators established a new classification of electronic phases protected by symmetry, with deep ties to topology and large impact.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele proposed the Z2 topological order; Molenkamp's group observed the effect in HgTe wells after the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal. BHZ and 3D topological insulator work (Fu, Kane, Mele, Hasan, Moore, Balents) complicate the credit.
assessment.maturity: Strongly confirmed in several materials, and the field is mature. Possibly the Thouless-Haldane 2016 prize reduces novelty.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2016 topological phase transitions prize
Several people with a strong claim (Zhang, Bernevig, Hasan) are outside the credited set

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The jamming picture unifies glasses, granular media and foams through a critical point with scaling and isostaticity, and is appealing to someone working in complex systems and stochastic physics. Original and conceptually clean.
assessment.attribution: Liu and Nagel's 1998 proposal of a jamming phase diagram is the common reference and the pair is a natural two-person configuration; O'Hern, Silbert, Wyart and others developed the critical scaling.
assessment.maturity: Numerics and experiments support the isostatic critical behaviour, but the connection to real glasses and thermal systems is still debated, so the interpretation is less settled than for others on my list.
uncertainties: Relevance to thermal glasses unresolved
Credit for subsequent critical-scaling work outside the credited names
Practical impact less direct
